Srini Pallia: 
Thank you, Abhishek. Good evening. Thank you all for joining us today. This quarter, demand 
environment has remained largely unchanged. Our clients remain focused on efficiency and 
productivity, while increasingly looking to accelerate AI adoption and drive long-term value. 
This balance between efficiency and growth is shaping demand across industries.  
Let me begin with what we see in our priority sectors. In BFSI, we continue to see strong 
momentum. Clients are focused on cost optimization, legacy modernization, and scaling agentic 
AI across their enterprise.  
Digital native and new-age firms are driving demand in our technology sector. Investments in 
custom silicon, design-to-manufacture, and physical AI are creating opportunities across the 
engineering value chain. We also see growth emerging across AI model ecosystems from model 
training and evaluation to execution. 
In EMR; Energy, Manufacturing, and Resources sector, we have seen some good wins in 
previous quarters, and those deals are ramping up. This sector continues to gain traction across 
markets. Specifically, I would like to call out CPS and engineering.

At the same time, cost pressures across payers and providers are creating new outsourcing 
opportunities. This, along with our differentiated platform-based offerings and including rising 
regulatory requirements, we are shaping our pipeline. 
Moving to our financial performance for the quarter. In quarter 2, our IT services revenue stood 
at $2.61 billion, flat sequentially and up 0.6% year-on-year in constant currency. Our operating 
margin for the quarter was 16.5%, an improvement of 0.5% compared to last quarter.  
Within our markets, three of our four SMUs, strategic market units, reported sequential growth. 
Americas 1 declined sequentially due to client-specific issues and softness in healthcare. 
Americas 2 grew sequentially, driven by EMR with encouraging momentum in BFSI.  
Europe grew sequentially and year-on-year, delivering broad-based growth led by BFSI, 
Consumer, and EMR. APMEA maintained strong traction, growing sequentially and year-on-
year. Growth was fueled by Consumer, Tech, and Comms. 
Coming to deal wins and pipeline. This quarter, we closed $2.6 billion in total contract value 
and signed nine large deals. Our bookings reflect a healthy mix of new businesses and expansion 
of existing engagements.  
Let me give an example of a consulting-led AI-powered transformation deal. A global financial 
institution engaged Wipro to accelerate its transformation through an AI-enabled operating 
model. Through this engagement, we'll modernize software development, drive greater 
efficiency across the life cycle, and scale AI-powered ways of working, resulting in faster 
execution, broader AI adoption, and an agile operating model for our client. This win, among 
others, including a large deal in Energy last quarter, reflects growing impact of our consulting-
led strategy in originating larger opportunities.  
Beyond large enterprises, we also see strong traction in deal wins and pipeline in the mid-market 
segment. These organizations understand that AI can be a force multiplier in scaling capabilities 
and redefining their competitive landscape. As an example, a global mid-market consumer 
products company selected us to accelerate their technology transformation by establishing an 
AI capability center in India.  
Through this engagement, we will scale engineering and technology operations to support ERP 
modernization, cloud-native platforms, and AI capabilities for our client. Outcome will drive 
innovation, improve engineering productivity, and strengthen global delivery model for our 
client.

outcome-based deals and driving nonlinear growth. This investment is already delivering results.

healthcare payer.

aviation, and asset-intensive industries. Combined with our AI agents and orchestration 
platform, these capabilities enable us to transform virtually any business workflow into an AI 
native workflow, helping our clients unlock new levels of productivity, speed, and business 
value.

devices, and design-to-manufacturing. In fact, these services and solutions position us well 
across the full AI value chain and help us capture opportunities that extend beyond traditional 
technology spend.

seasonal furloughs. We are guiding for a sequential IT services revenue growth of minus 1.5% 
to plus 0.5% in constant currency.  
Despite a challenging macro environment, our business remains resilient. We are very 
encouraged by emerging opportunities across markets. AI will expand new growth avenues and 
accelerate demand for higher-value transformation. Signs of this are already evident in the 
momentum we are seeing across our new AI services.
